DEFECT (R5 'usable on a 375px wide phone ... controls reachable', and the binding design in architecture.md section 5 lines 142-144): every task checkbox has too small a tap target. style.css lines 120-126 set `.todo-item .toggle { width: 1.75rem; height: 1.75rem; margin: 0.5rem 0.25rem; }`, which is 28x28 CSS px. app.js lines 152-156 and 168 add the checkbox directly to the li with only an aria-label and no wrapping <label>. Margin does not count as tap area, so the target stays 28x28. architecture.md asks for every visible checkbox to be >= 44x44 CSS px and says the 1.75rem checkbox should sit 'inside a padded label'. All other controls (#new-todo, #add-btn, the filter buttons, button.delete) have min-height/min-width 44px; only the checkbox misses it.

Why the checks miss this defect: checks/browser-check.mjs (around lines 640-670) measures max(control box, label box) and, per architecture.md, only enforces a 24x24 hard minimum. A 28x28 checkbox therefore passes T5/T6 even though it misses the 44x44 design target. A passing check here would not prove the phone-usability part of R5.

Secondary observation (no failing requirement): app.js line 156 always sets aria-label 'Mark <text> done', even when the task is already done, so the accessible name is misleading after ticking. The architecture allows this exact text (line 61), so I am noting it, not counting it as a defect against R2.

Candidate defect (code inspection only, not reproduced in a browser): /home/user/probes/web-todo/app.js render() at lines 143-185 clears and rebuilds the entire #todo-list on every commit. commit() at lines 99-102 calls it after toggle() (lines 113-118) and remove() (lines 120-125). The focused checkbox or delete button is destroyed, so keyboard focus drops to the document body and a keyboard user has to re-tab from the top of the page after each toggle or delete. This is an indirect conflict with R5 'controls reachable' and with R2 'each task has a checkbox that toggles done' when operated from the keyboard. The requirement text does not state focus retention explicitly, so the mapping is a judgment call and needs a real Chromium Tab/Space check to confirm.

Secondary observation, not claimed as a defect: with the Done filter active, add() (lines 104-111) appends an active task that is not shown, so the user sees no feedback from pressing Enter. R1 says typing and pressing Enter 'appends a task', and the task is appended to state, so this is ambiguous rather than a clear violation. Filter-matching behaviour for R3 looks correct in code.

Other code-level checks that look correct on reading: whitespace trim and empty-input rejection in add() (R1); corrupted localStorage is caught and normalized in load()/normalize() with a rewrite of repaired state (R4); the active filter is persisted through the filter field; the counter counts !done items (R3); the done style uses line-through and a grey colour (R2); the layout has a 1rem mobile padding, flex-wrap filters and overflow-wrap on text (R5). None of these was tested in a browser here.

Existing evidence in .autodev/evidence (T1 test/behavior reports and a visual report) lists PASS assertions for the current product. The app.js, index.html and style.css sizes (6228, 1013, 2636 bytes) match the build manifest sizes. Those reports were not re-run by this probe and were not treated as current verification. The backlog still shows T1 UNVERIFIED and current-task stage IDLE, so the harness has not advanced the gate on the existing T1 evidence.
